clue.text: Smooth call by actor at royal house

parts.note: to smooth wood is to sand it
to call someone is to ring them
a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: An actor with a smooth voice makes a call at a royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandringham in Norfolk is a country residence of the British monarch, so it is a royal estate.

clue.text: Horrify a sound apostle

indicators.note: sound tells us to take the spoken form of the following word rather than its spelling

parts.note: Paul is the apostle who wrote many New Testament letters

explanation.surface: A trustworthy apostle somehow manages to horrify people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but it signals that the apostle PAUL is heard, giving the spelling PPAL after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To horrify someone is to shock and dismay them, a close synonym.

clue.text: Gives a note in to teachers

indicators.note: in places the note pieces within the word for teachers

parts.note: dons are university teachers
te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a note to the teaching staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give something, typically to a cause, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Tell one's playing well

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a player is on good form.
explanation.definitionFit: Inform means tell; a sportsperson playing well is said to be in form.

clue.text: Talking turkey?

parts.note: the idiom means speaking frankly, but read literally it is a turkey making its noise

explanation.surface: Someone is speaking frankly about business.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobbling is the throaty call a turkey makes, its form of speech.

clue.text: Song bringing up death of Theseus's lover

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up means the word for death is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: death is the end of life

explanation.surface: A song recalls the death of the hero Theseus's beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ariadne helped Theseus escape the labyrinth and became his lover.

clue.text: Comprehensive settlement for our small planet

parts.note: global means all-embracing or comprehensive
a village is a small settlement

explanation.surface: A complete deal is struck to protect the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the world seen as one small interconnected community thanks to modern communications.

clue.text: May find what's wrong with instrument

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of the word what are out of order

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter, leaving the four letters of what
a horn is a brass musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone might discover what is faulty with a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like a verb or the month, but it is the name of a flowering shrub; 'wrong' turns WHAT into HAWT.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawthorn is commonly called may, after the month it blossoms.

clue.text: Give way here animal in transit

parts.note: a zebra is a striped African animal
a crossing is a passage across, a transit

explanation.surface: Drivers must yield where an animal is on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: A zebra crossing is a British pedestrian crossing marked with black and white stripes, where drivers must stop for people on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: At this striped crossing motorists must yield to pedestrians, so it is a place to stop for walkers.

clue.text: Briefly line up in plant

parts.note: briefly means abbreviated, and L is the short form of line
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Quickly get people to queue inside a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden flower with tall spikes of blooms.

clue.text: Construct a brief act in play

indicators.note: in play suggests the letters are moving around freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone builds a short scene within a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: To fabricate is to make or put together, the same as to construct.

clue.text: Labour returned-I afterwards get in with both sides'agreement

indicators.note: get in means the following pieces enter the reversed party name
returned tells us to read the abbreviation for Labour backwards

parts.note: Lab is the usual short form of the British Labour Party
later means afterwards

explanation.surface: Labour came back and later took power with cross-party support.
explanation.definitionFit: A bilateral deal is made by two parties together, each side consenting.

clue.text: Prevent animals eating last of harvest

indicators.note: eating means the animals take something inside them

parts.note: deer are animals

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of harvest

explanation.surface: Stop wild beasts from consuming the end of the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage or stop an action, a synonym of prevent.

clue.text: Commander overcome by desire — a plaguey creature

indicators.note: overcome by means the commander is surrounded by the desire

parts.note: lust is strong desire
OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: An officer is consumed by longing for a pestilent insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plaguey' points to the biblical plague of these insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusts swarm in vast numbers and devastate crops, as in the plagues of Egypt.

clue.text: Share of proceeds I offer? Stop it!

parts.note: a cut is a share of the profits
to tout is to offer goods for sale persistently

explanation.surface: Someone offering a share of the takings is told to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a curt command to cease doing something.

clue.text: Upper-class and rich — one sadly is cowardly

parts.note: U is the classic abbreviation for upper-class

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters of the following words are in a sorry state, rearranged

explanation.surface: A wealthy aristocrat is unfortunately a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' reads as emotional commentary on the rich aristocrat, but it is the anagram signal; 'and' and 'is' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Unheroic means lacking courage or nobility, the opposite of brave.

clue.text: Islands can attract group of stars

parts.note: Aries is a constellation, the Ram

explanation.surface: Some islands can draw a constellation of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canaries are a Spanish archipelago off north-west Africa.

clue.text: Break spell

explanation.surface: Interrupt a magical incantation.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a pause in a performance, and also a period of time.

clue.text: High status took precedence, and caused grievance

parts.note: rank is a high position in society
to have led is to have come first

explanation.surface: Someone of high standing pulled rank and upset people.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankled caused lasting resentment or bitterness.

clue.text: Country finally changed this dictator

indicators.note: finally changed means the last letter of the country is swapped for another

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: A nation was ultimately transformed by its dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter goes in: the final E of FRANCE becomes O.
explanation.definitionFit: General Franco ruled Spain as a military dictator from 1939 to 1975.

clue.text: Free issue

explanation.surface: Something handed out without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To release is to set free, and a release is something issued, like a record or statement.

clue.text: Hard work on an advertising catch-phrase

parts.note: a slog is a spell of hard work

explanation.surface: Much effort goes into writing an advertising line.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a memorable motto used in marketing.

clue.text: Tongue, pound a can

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for the pound sterling
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone's tongue might hit a can hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is a language, and tongue means language.

clue.text: Ball-play is deficient? Not usually, with them

indicators.note: play suggests the letters of ball are moved about

parts.note: lacks means is deficient or wanting

explanation.surface: Asks whether ball skills are poor, and answers that they rarely are for this side.
explanation.walkthrough: The ALL BLACKS are New Zealand's national rugby team, famous for skilful ball-handling; 'play' turns BALL into ALL. The second half defines them as the side whose ball play is seldom deficient.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Zealand rugby side are renowned for skill, so poor handling is rare with them.

clue.text: Youngster admonished, concealing money

indicators.note: concealing means the word for admonished hides something inside it

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, meaning scolded
L stands for pound, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A young person is told off for hiding cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A child is a young person.

clue.text: Demanding porridge, then fish

parts.note: gruel is a thin porridge
ling is an edible fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone insists on porridge followed by fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruelling means exhausting and demanding of great effort.

clue.text: Strange falsehood in article

indicators.note: in places the falsehood within the article

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a lie is a falsehood

explanation.surface: A peculiar untruth is printed in a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign or unfamiliar, hence strange.

clue.text: Not even Chopin's friend finishes such a miscellany

parts.note: an odd number is one that is not even
George Sand, the French novelist, was Chopin's companion
ends are finishes

explanation.surface: An uneven tale of Chopin's companion completes a varied collection.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a jumble of assorted leftover items, a miscellany.
